facts.text: WET, the rooftop pool on the 76th floor, has panoramic city and harbor views.
facts.excerpt: Head to WET®, our 76th floor rooftop swimming pool, a cool 211 meters (692 feet) above ground where you can dip in the water or just lounge on a deck chair surrounded by panoramic city and harbor views.

facts.text: The hotel was designed by two firms around an enchanted forest theme.
facts.excerpt: W Hong Kong was designed in tandem by 2 design firms to create an enchanted forest theme.

facts.text: The glass lobby has oversized insect sculptures, tree trunk-like columns and rows of LED twig lights.
facts.excerpt: The all-glass lobby of the W Hong Kong transports travelers into an enchanted forest, with outsize insect sculptures, a textured Japanese “sand” wall, tree trunk-like columns, and rows of LED twig lights.

facts.text: Bliss Spa has couple suites and treatment rooms overlooking the harbor.
facts.excerpt: Bliss® Spa boasts over 14,500 square feet of relaxation facilities with two luxury couple suites and nine treatment rooms overlooking the harbor.

facts.text: The 73rd-floor heat and water area has a harbor-view vitality pool, an aroma steam room and a dry sauna.
facts.excerpt: Location: 73/F, W Hong Kong Experience includes: Harbor view vitality pool/experience shower/aroma steam room/dry sauna.

facts.text: Use of the heat and water area is included with spa services other than nail care and waxing.
facts.excerpt: Use of heat & water experience on the 73rd floor is included with all spa services except nail care and poetic waxing.

facts.text: Rooms and suites were designed by g+a and Glamorous in eight different styles.
facts.excerpt: our extravagant hotel rooms and suites were designed by g+a and Glamorous in eight different styles.

facts.text: Rooms have views of the cityscape, harbor or waterfront.
facts.excerpt: Wake up to warm rays of natural light in your hotel room, which features views of the Hong Kong cityscape, harbor or waterfront.

facts.text: In the suites, all bathrooms get natural light and two-thirds have harbor views.
facts.excerpt: Our suites cater foremost to the whims of corporate guests as well as to the playful sensibilities of the weekender. All bathrooms settle in natural light and 2/3 of them have harbor views.

facts.text: The hotel is near Kowloon Station, with easy access to the Airport Express and mainland China.
facts.excerpt: With our location near Kowloon Station, you have easy access to Airport Express, mainland China and Hong Kong's best sites and bites.

facts.text: The hotel is connected to the Elements mall.
facts.excerpt: navigate the labyrinthine Elements mall (connected to the hotel)

facts.text: Reception is on the sixth floor, reached by a glass bubble lift with glimpses of the shipping port.
facts.excerpt: The reception is set on the sixth floor, so you’ll ride a glass bubble lift, catching a glimpse of the fascinating shipping port (piled high with colorful cargo containers) along the way.

facts.text: The WET Deck has a mosaic mural behind its lounge chairs and views of the harbor.
facts.excerpt: Admire the fantastic mosaic mural behind the lounge chairs or gaze at electrifying views of Hong Kong Harbor.

facts.text: KITCHEN serves an international buffet with handmade dim sum, sushi and seafood.
facts.excerpt: Indulge in our whimsical international buffet with everything from handmade dim sum and sushi to generous heaps of fresh seafood, hearty salads, decadent desserts, and more gourmet delights.

facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says travelers focused on sightseeing in Tsim Sha Tsui, Central or the outlying islands may find the neighborhood overly commercial.
facts.excerpt: Those aiming to spend their time visiting the cultural sites in Tsim Sha Tsui, Central, or the outlying islands might find the neighborhood (or lack thereof) overly commercial.

facts.text: The restaurants are popular with locals, so communal areas often mix guests and neighborhood residents.
facts.excerpt: As it turns out, the restaurants are extremely popular with locals, so the communal areas often see a mix of guests and neighborhood residents.
